proposal.title: Naeorvlin: a build comparison service
proposal.summary: Naeorvlin builds a build comparison service for distributors of free software.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Users cannot check that a binary was built from the source it claims. Distributors of free software depend on reproducible builds every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a build comparison service called Naeorvlin. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Reproducible builds is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/naeorvlin/naeorvlin, which 268 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on reproducible builds for 9 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/naeorvlin/naeorvlin. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 48200.00 EUR for 79 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Users cannot check that a binary was built from the source it claims. Distributors of free software depend on reproducible builds every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a build comparison service called Naeorvlin. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Reproducible builds is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/naeorvlin/naeorvlin, which 268 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on reproducible builds for 9 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/naeorvlin/naeorvlin. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 48200.00 EUR for 79 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
